column1: # capability-parity.tsv — one row per STAGED-LANE CAPABILITY, with its recorded disposition.
#   capability <TAB> staged implementation path(s) <TAB> disposition <TAB> lean home / decision note
# WHY THIS EXISTS: #348 deletes the staged lane, and its parity story is per-ARTIFACT (an orphan
# check keyed on deleted paths). A behavior whose only implementation lives inside a stage doc is
# therefore deletable with nothing red and no record that the deletion was a decision. This file
# is that record, and tools/capability-parity-check.sh is what makes #348's deletions answerable
# REGISTER-WORTHY iff removing the behavior changes what a CONSUMER RUN produces or verifies — an
# artifact, a gate verdict, a review dimension — as opposed to how the run choreographs itself.
# Rows are behavior-level, not file-level: one capability may be implemented by a stage doc plus
# several tools and workflow scripts, and the path cell enumerates ALL of them, so a tools-file
# deletion is covered via its owning behavior.
#   ported          the behavior has a lean implementation that is not the staged one
#   already-covered a lean-native home already provides it; the note names that home
#   dropped         a real capability deliberately given no lean home; the note says where a
#                   consumer that wants it goes instead
#   choreography    dies with the stages BY NATURE (stage-progression bookkeeping). The parent's
#                   rule requires that death to be a RECORDED decision, which is why this is a
#                   first-class machine-readable value and not a synonym for `dropped`.
# ROWS ARE PERMANENT RECORD. A row is never removed when its staged paths die — the whole point is
# that the disposition outlives the implementation. The guard's stages-file coverage clause becomes
# vacuous once #348 lands, by design; the shape/enum lint does not.
# SEEDED vs PROPOSED: four rows carry dispositions settled at intake (mutation gate, visual
# capture, doc update, design-fidelity + a11y routing). Every other row was proposed by the
# stage-1..10 walk and ratified by review at the PR that introduced it.
# CONFIG-KEY CONSEQUENCES ride in the note cell (unitTestScope, gates.mutation, testFile,
# stageParams.visualCapture, stageParams.inertPattern, planGates, implementDelegates) so the
# config-schema assessment can execute retirement under the dead-key pattern. No key is retired
# HERE — this file records the fate, the retirement happens in the schema and config-lint.
# Executed so far: stageParams.visualCapture (#348); stageWorkflows, implementDelegates and
# planGates (#569). The `dropped` rows below keep their disposition and now name the PR that
# carried it out, so a reader can tell a proposal from a completed retirement.

column4: lean-gate.sh `claim` makes the same two bot writes (label swap + claim marker) and check-lean-chain.sh gates the claim comment at the merge boundary. claim-issue.sh itself is shared, not stage-owned.

No lean equivalent: nothing in build-lean/ reads a Predecessor:/Successor: trailer, so a successor queued early is claimable and the predecessor's PR carries no promotion line. A consumer wanting the ordering enforces it by not labelling the successor until the predecessor merges — which is already the routine path, since a sequential decomposition leaves blocked successors out of the queue.

intake-toolkit:intake / intake-orchestrator / spec-reviewer / codebase-explorer survive independently of the stages, and lean makes paid-off intake a PRECONDITION (the queue label at checklist step 1) rather than an in-run stage. The readRoot pin that grounds the fan-out at origin/<baseBranch> rides with intake-review.mjs, not with the stage doc.

The lean spec's `## Design` section is the armament (handoff link + RS-n rows, or the explicit `Design: none — <reason>` disarm), state-locked once milestone 3 arms. lean-gate.sh reads the design axis from config `design.*` directly; no per-run detection step is needed.

The COMMITTED lean spec is the run-authoritative definition of done — milestone 1 asserts at least one numbered AC-n, and review-lean scores every AC-n against the diff. Being committed is what makes it immune to later ticket edits, which is exactly what the statectl snapshot bought.

The whole ticketTag -> targetRepos -> per-repo worktree/verify/review/PR fan-out has no lean counterpart: nothing in build-lean/ mentions targetRepos, and lean-gate.sh works exactly one repo's worktree (its design.liveRender.cwd arm refuses a sibling checkout in those words). A pair consumer runs the lean lane once per repo. topology.type: be-fe-pair stays a valid config shape for other readers; whether it survives is #348's assessment.

column1: worktree and branch creation from the configured base
column4: Checklist step 3 mandates a worktree on <lean prefix><issue> cut from the configured base; branch-prefix.sh owns the namespace, `lean-gate.sh entry` sweeps abandoned lane worktrees and `teardown` destroys this run's (never the branch).

column1: committed plan artifact as the definition of done
column4: The lean spec at <plansDir>/<repo>-<issue>-lean.md is the same artifact one rung simpler: committed on the branch, linked from the PR body (milestone 5 asserts the link), and gated for existence at milestone 1.

Deliberate. Milestone 1 asserts the spec exists and names at least one AC-n; it asserts nothing about ten required sections, [NEW]/[UNVERIFIED] grounding tags, or an AC traceability table. The lean posture is that a spec is judged by the review half against the diff, not by a section census — and the 60-line SKILL cap exists to stop exactly this kind of process accretion returning.

The LEDGER CONTRACT itself survives outside the stages (intake-toolkit:interviewing-baseline owns the schema; exitplan-ledger-gate.sh enforces it at plan exit). What dies is the mechanical hydration check — plan-lint Check 6 requiring every backing D-n row copied verbatim into the plan. Lean treats a pre-flight <issue>-ledger.md as binding input by prose (checklist step 4), ungated.

CORRECTED (#574): this row previously read `already-covered` on the claim that the engines are dispatched by scriptPath rather than by the stage. That claim was false — the scriptPath dispatch lived in stages/3-write-plan.md and stages/5-implement.md and died with them, so design-sync.mjs and figma.mjs ship with NO dispatcher. The design-faithful/figma-faithful SKILLS do survive; the produce ENGINES are unreachable. Re-wire or retire is tracked in #574. Original note follows: design-toolkit:design-faithful-spec / figma-faithful-spec survive as skills and the engines are dispatched by scriptPath, not by the stage. Lean's gated design artifact is the spec's RS-n table plus milestone 3's render receipt at <plansDir>/<key>-lean-renders.md, which is what the review half's fidelity scoring binds to.

Same precedent as the doc-update row: review-toolkit:plan-reviewer survives as an on-demand agent, and lean's checklist calls the elicitation surfaces a pool, none mandated. There is no pre-implementation gate in the lean lane — the spec is judged at the merge boundary by review-lean, after the diff exists.

Config key `planGates` has no lean reader. Lean's extension seam is `extraLanes`, which adds VERIFY lanes at milestone 3; there is no additive plan-gate seam because there is no plan gate to be additive to. RETIRED in #569: the key is out of the schema and config-lint rejects it by name; the shape survives as a design record in docs/extending.md §3.8.

CORRECTED (#574): `ported` overstated this. tools/mutation-sweep.sh mutates SHELL GUARDS; it is not the LLM-proposed-mutants-over-co-located-unit-tests capability mutation-gate.mjs implements, and mutation-gate.mjs has had no dispatcher since #348 deleted stages/5-implement.md. The consumer-facing half of that gap is #482. Tracked in #574. Original note follows: SEEDED. Ported to the repo-carried tools/mutation-sweep.sh seam: lean-gate.sh's D-18 block is the executor (`bash tools/mutation-sweep.sh --mode pr --base origin/<baseBranch>`; rc!=0 reds milestone-3), running when the target repo carries the sweep and skipping with a notice when it does not. A starter recipe for consumer repos whose mutation surface is co-located unit tests is deliberately out of scope here (follow-up candidate). Config keys `unitTestScope`, `gates.mutation` and `testFile` have zero readers under lean — retirement candidates for #348.

Lean is outcome-gated and silent on HOW the diff is produced, so a session may dispatch the same delegate agent by choice. What has no lean home is the declared mechanism: config-routed surface->agent matching with a pre-flight fail-closed resolution check. Config key `implementDelegates` was RETIRED in #569: out of the schema, rejected by name at config-lint, shape kept as a design record in docs/extending.md §3.7. What a session chooses to dispatch is unaffected; the declared, pre-flight-validated routing is what is gone.

CORRECTED (#574): milestone 3's render lane runs the configured design.liveRender.command and is a real gate, but it does NOT dispatch design-sync.mjs or figma.mjs — those engines have no caller since #348. What is covered is the render RECEIPT, not the design-faithful implement engine. Tracked in #574. Original note follows: Milestone 3's render lane is the lean home and is strictly stronger: it runs config `design.liveRender.command` per RS-n row, hashes the PNGs into a committed receipt, refuses an armed spec with no configured harness, and (milestone 4) refuses a receipt whose rendered_from no longer matches the branch. The staged gate degraded to a non-blocking `render-verify-unavailable` when unconfigured.

Milestone 3 runs the config commands table directly — setup lanes, lint, typecheck, test, extraLanes with the same `when` glob dialect, the same SEAM_SCRUB env hermeticity (pinned verbatim in scripts/lockstep-manifest.tsv), and a fix budget of 3 attempts per milestone with a hard stop at rc=4 in place of verifyctl's per-class budget and circuit breaker.

Deliberate, and stated as such in lean-gate.sh's milestone-3 header: no inert lane, because in a repo whose diffs are mostly shell and markdown the lane would skip the suite on exactly the changes that need it most. is-inert-diff.sh itself survives — the pre-commit type-check hook and config-grill.sh both read it — so only the verify-lane skip dies. Config key `stageParams.inertPattern` is a retirement candidate for #348.

No lean counterpart: nothing in build-lean/ runs an advisory cleanup pass, and there is no once-per-run guard, apply-scope rule or safety-net re-verify. Reuse/simplification findings reach the lean lane through the review half instead, as ordinary review findings a fix round addresses.

SEEDED. Smoke-route screenshots die with the stages as choreography would, but this is a recorded drop of a real capability, not a choreography death. `extraLanes` is the documented home for a consumer-carried screenshot lane. Config key `stageParams.visualCapture.*` is a retirement candidate for #348.

SEEDED. The review-toolkit:doc-updater agent survives independently and stays on-demand; a consumer wanting a mandatory check wires it via `extraLanes` or review policy. Lean's own obligation is the AC-scoped one: a change that makes docs stale needs an explicit doc AC-n.

No lean mechanical reconciliation of changed files against the spec's affected/out-of-scope path lists. The lean analog is judgment at the merge boundary: review-lean scores each AC-n against the diff and treats a spec amended after the fact to match the diff as itself a blocker.

The structured {kind, planSection, file, note} ledger with its closed kind enum has no lean reader. Lean's disclosure channel is narrower and differently shaped: the P9 intent-gap record (schema in intake-toolkit:interviewing-baseline), which check-lean-chain.sh refuses when `ratified: no`, plus whatever the PR body discloses. A plan-vs-diff divergence that is not also an unratified decision has no gated home.

column1: code-review fan-out panel and bounded round loop
column4: review-lean is the lean home and review-lead is its stated implementation. The rounds round-trip through committed artifacts instead of an in-session loop, and lean-gate.sh binds each verdict to a reviewed_patch_id with an inheritance chain, so a later round reads the delta rather than re-reading the branch. The round loop's BOUND is a separate capability and is dispositioned separately in the next row — what is already-covered here is the fan-out and the round-trip, not what exhausting the cap produces.

The 3-round cap's terminal path applies the `needs-deep-review` label, writes `codeReviewExhausted` to state, and renders an **Outstanding Review Blockers** section into the PR body — plus the two sibling short-circuits that reuse it (scope-blocker-no-code-remedy, review-void-zero-coverage). Those are consumer-visible produced artifacts: a label and a PR section telling a human the diff shipped with blockers nobody cleared. Lean has no reader for any of the three tokens and neither SKILL declares a round cap — a lean run simply keeps spending rounds. A consumer that wants the signal wires it as repository policy on the PR (label + required review), not in the lane. Distinct from the voided-round row below, which covers the DARK panel and is stricter under lean.

SEEDED. plugins/review-toolkit/skills/review-lead/SKILL.md reads `stageParams.webComponentGlobs` itself, lean reaches review-lead through the review half, and lean-gate.sh carries a `--fidelity` verdict flag that milestone 4 requires to be `pass` on an armed run.

review-lean step 5c is the lean contract and is stricter: an all-dark panel is handed back with NO verdict record written and the round not spent, and check-lean-chain.sh treats an absent record as already a violation, so a voided round cannot merge.

review-lean scores every numbered AC-n in the committed spec as satisfied / unsatisfied / undeterminable and treats any unmet AC-n as a blocker. review-toolkit:scope-completeness-reviewer survives as an agent review-lead may select.

column1: consolidated report as a code-host artifact
column4: review-lean step 8 posts the findings as one PR comment through the bot wrapper, and step 6/7 commit the verdict record to the branch — a stronger version of the same property, since the record is what milestone 4 and the merge boundary read.

Milestone 5 gates the externally-visible artifacts directly: an open, non-draft PR carrying `Closes #<issue>` (or `Closes [<KEY>]` under a `Jira Items` heading) and a link to the committed spec. Lean deliberately opens READY rather than draft — the committed verdict record, not draft status, is what carries review state.

Checklist step 7 computes it once via `pipeline-cost-block.sh --stateless` and appends it to the PR description; step 9 repeats the same block in the closing comment. The `--stateless` mode is what removes the statectl state file from the path.

The gitignored <issue>-report.md and the mark-completed gate that required it have no lean counterpart. The operator now reads the run on the surfaces milestone 5 gates — the PR body and the closing comment — which is where a reviewer looks anyway; what is lost is the local artifact that survived a mid-response disconnect.

No pre-push overlap check in the lean lane. Conflict detection is the code host's and CI's, and lean's resume guidance is to rebase when the base moved; the verdict's patch-id binding then tells the run whether the rebase cost a round (a replay does not, a conflict resolution does).

column1: post-run eval and retro corpus record
column4: tools/retro-corpus.sh already detects the lean artifact shape structurally (a verdict_record: header key) rather than by filename, so lean runs enter the corpus that pipeline-retro and perf-retro read. The statectl-shaped <issue>-eval.json and the mark-completed gate that required it belong to the state machine — see the stage-progression row.

`lean-gate.sh teardown` destroys this run's worktree (never the branch) or says why it kept it, and `lean-gate.sh entry` sweeps lane worktrees whose PR is no longer open — covering the abandoned runs the staged Stage 10 never reached.

Dies with the stages by nature: set-stage started/completed writes, stage checkpoints, stage-file-read receipts, completion-evidence preconditions, the failureContext reason enum, crash-recovery resume, and the waiver acceptance flow that exists only because those preconditions can be forced. All of it exists to sequence stages. Lean's equivalent surface is the progress file, which records milestone verdicts rather than stage lifecycle.

Dies with the stages by nature: the stage:/status: marker comments and their comment-add receipts narrate stage progression, so there is nothing left to narrate. Lean makes exactly two tracker writes per clean run by design (the claim comment and the closing comment), and milestone 5 gates the closing one on referencing the verdict record.
